outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: The specific game chosen (EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27) is fine as long as it truly came from “Best sellers.” Minor wording/formatting in the report would not matter.

Critical issues: (1) Missing required deliverable: the agent did not provide the publisher. The task explicitly requires reporting publisher, developer, and release date; providing only 2 of 3 is not sufficient. While the agent appropriately avoided fabricating the publisher, the user still doesn’t get the full requested info. (2) “Best sellers” provenance is not evidenced: the screenshots/DOM provided start at the product page and do not show any “Best sellers” list/section or the selection step. So, from the available ground-truth evidence, we cannot confirm the game was actually found under “Best sellers” as requested.

What was achieved: The agent did open an Xbox.com product page for EA SPORTS™ Madden NFL 27, and the screenshots support “Developed by: Tiburon” and “Release date: 8/13/2026.” Constraints were respected (no sign-in, no purchase/download). However, because the agent cannot supply the publisher and cannot substantiate that the game came from a “Best sellers” section, the primary intent is not met from an average user’s perspective (they asked for a complete 3-field report for a best-seller game).
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to use Xbox.com to pick any game that appears in a “Best sellers” section, open that game’s product page, and report three specific metadata fields from that page: publisher, developer, and release date. A reasonable user would be flexible about which best-selling game is chosen, but not flexible about missing one of the three required fields or using a game that can’t be tied to “Best sellers.”
